--- PART 1/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Parent slot 3 fitness 269.88 best? Actually cumulative: slot3 269.88, slot4 267.60, slot10 266.75, slot11 265.99, slot8 264.21. Need new strategy improving parent."
STRATEGY: Parent is a TFT2-style strategy: first C, defects if opponent defections >=3 and >= n//2, defects after two consecutive opponent D, defects when remaining<=2, and after mutual D defects with 0.7 probability. The trace simulates this parent against population slots (slot0, slot2, slot6, slot8, TFT, always-D, always-C) and considers changes: faster retaliation, endgame only last round, and probing to exploit always-C.

--- PART 2/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The fitness given is cumulative training fitness, likely average over matches. Parent slot3 got 269.88. The best slot0 got 248. Parent is highest. So parent is already best. We need improve slightly."
STRATEGY: Parent is a TFT2-style policy: starts C, defects if opponent's last two actions were D, and permanently-ish defects when opp_defections >= 3 and >= n//2; it also defects when remaining <= 2. The trace simulates it against AlwaysC, TFT, Grim, slot0, slot6, and parent-vs-parent, and proposes removing the remaining<=2 endgame defect so it only defects on the final round.

--- PART 3/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Given all this, the parent is already well-designed. The most promising improvement is the endgame."
STRATEGY: Parent cooperates first, defects if opponent has ≥3 defections and ≥ half the rounds, defects after two consecutive opponent defections, randomly defects 70% after mutual defection, and defects in the last two rounds. The trace simulates this parent against TFT-like, exploitative, and defector opponents, then proposes removing the unconditional second-to-last-round defect and adding a last-round-only defect.

--- PART 4/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Wait, the original parent had `remaining = 100 - n; if remaining <= 2: return 'D'`. That means it defected at n=98 and n=99. We removed that and added `if n == 99: return 'D'`."
STRATEGY: Parent defects unconditionally at n=98 and n=99 via remaining<=2. Simulated removing the n=98 unconditional defect while keeping n=99 defect, plus global defection-rate trigger and 0.7 random defection after mutual D. Changed by dropping the n=98 unconditional defect and adding `if n == 99: return 'D'`.
